  continuous: aspect_deg (Direction the ground faces, i.e. the compass bearing of steepest DESCENT, degrees clockwise from north (0 = faces north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west), Horn 3x3 finite difference on the 2 m elevation (about 6 m support), same gradient as slope_2m. 'North-facing' means aspect_deg within 45 deg of 0 (or aspect_class N / NE / NW)); curvature_plan (Curvature of the contour line across the slope (spurs / ridges diverge = positive, gullies / hollows converge = negative), Zevenbergen and Thorne 3x3 partial-quartic, computed on the elevation after Gaussian smoothing (sigma 5 m = 2.5 cells, kernel truncated at 3 sigma = 15 m radius, full width at half maximum about 12 m) to remove 1-2 m stereo noise; features narrower than roughly 10-15 m are suppressed. Sign convention (both layers): POSITIVE = convex (crest, spur, dome), NEGATIVE = concave (hollow, valley, bowl); values are 1/m, so a paraboloid z = a r^2 gives -2a. (Zevenbergen and Thorne's raw plan-curvature formula has the opposite sign to their profile formula; plan is flipped here so both read the same way.) ); curvature_profile (Curvature of the surface along the downslope direction (convex breaks of slope at the top of scarps = positive, concave bases = negative), Zevenbergen and Thorne 3x3 partial-quartic, computed on the elevation after Gaussian smoothing (sigma 5 m = 2.5 cells, kernel truncated at 3 sigma = 15 m radius, full width at half maximum about 12 m) to remove 1-2 m stereo noise; features narrower than roughly 10-15 m are suppressed. Sign convention (both layers): POSITIVE = convex (crest, spur, dome), NEGATIVE = concave (hollow, valley, bowl); values are 1/m, so a paraboloid z = a r^2 gives -2a. (Zevenbergen and Thorne's raw plan-curvature formula has the opposite sign to their profile formula; plan is flipped here so both read the same way.) ); dist_to_traverse_m (Euclidean distance from the cell centre to the nearest point of the Perseverance traverse line (traverse.geojson, NASA MMGIS drive segments, straight lines between published vertices)); dist_to_unit_contact_m (Euclidean distance from the cell centre to the nearest boundary between two different mapped geologic units (cells touching a different known unit; the boundary with 'no polygon' is not a contact)); elevation (Surface elevation above the MOLA areoid (delta-geoid corrected), 1 m HiRISE stereo DTM averaged to 2 m; CTX 20 m DTM (bilinear) where HiRISE has no data); local_relief_200m (Maximum minus minimum elevation within 200 m of each cell: highlights large landforms (delta-front scarps, crater rim, mesa edges) against flat floor); local_relief_50m (Maximum minus minimum elevation within 50 m (disc, centre to cell-centre distance) of each cell: a proxy for the height of a scarp, cliff or incised wall in the neighbourhood); mineral_diversity_100m (Number of distinct CRISM mineral layers (of 7: carbonate, olivine, Fe/Mg-smectite, high-Ca pyroxene, low-Ca pyroxene, kaolinite, Mg-smectite-2) with at least one cell of tier >= weak_orbital within 100 m (integer stored as float). Counts layers, not independent minerals: mixed prototypes appear in more than one layer, and pyroxene/smectite variants count separately); outcrop_exposure (Height proxy for an exposed vertical section: local_relief_50m where at least 2% of the cells within 50 m have slope_2m >= 25 degrees (a steep face is actually present in the window), else 0. High values mean tall steep walls nearby, the places where stratigraphy can be seen in section); rough_5x5 (Standard deviation of elevation in a 5x5 cell (10 m) window, no plane removal, so on tilted ground it includes the slope contribution); slope_2m (Surface slope from the 2 m elevation, Horn 3x3 finite difference (about 6 m support)); tpi_50m (Cell elevation minus the mean elevation of the other cells within 50 m (disc, centre excluded) on the 2 m grid. Unit is metres; includes the slope contribution (a smooth 30 deg ramp has a high TRI)); unit_diversity_100m (Number of distinct mapped geologic units having at least one cell within 100 m of the cell (integer stored as float). 1 = deep inside one unit, 2+ = near a contact, 3+ = junctions)

data.result:
slope_2m [continuous] Slope over 2 m grid (Horn), units: degrees
Measures: Surface slope from the 2 m elevation, Horn 3x3 finite difference (about 6 m support).
Does NOT measure: Slopes of features smaller than about 4-6 m (individual rocks, small ripples); direction of slope.
Quality: NaN where any of 3x3 neighbours is unknown. Computed on CTX-filled or seam-suspect elevation where quality_flag != hirise_dtm; those values are retained but unreliable. Cells are class 0 only if every elevation in their 5x5 window is HiRISE data without suspected seam artefacts; see quality_flag. Values near CTX fill or seam suspects are kept (never altered) but flagged.
Range 0.00124 to 69.3, median 3.4.
Coverage: 100% of cells have data (rest unknown, never treated as safe or absent).
Resolution: 2 m. Source: MRO/HiRISE (stereo DTM, MOLA-registered), Fergason et al. 2020, USGS Astrogeology, doi:10.5066/P9REJ9JN.
